prompts.code-review: Review Sprout's code for bugs and problems.
prompts.compliance-review: Review Sprout for data protection problems. It operates in Nigeria.
prompts.ai-feature-review: Review Sprout's plant identification feature, which uses an AI service.
prompts.data-migration-review: Review how Sprout stores data on the device, and what happens to that data when the app updates.
prompts.design-review: Review Sprout against its design system.

defects.title: Version 2 deletes the journal's old table without moving its entries across, so every person loses their journal

locations.match: this.version(2).stores({ plants: "++id, name, room, position", entries: null, journal: "++id, plantId, at" });

defects.title: The app never asks the browser to keep its data, so the browser may delete the only copy when space runs short
The service worker always serves its cached copy of the app, so people never get an update
Identifying a plant sends the original photo, with where it was taken, without telling the person
The identification service's key is built into the web app, where anyone can read it
The identification call has no timeout and never checks for a failed response

locations.match: const response = await fetch(url, { method: "POST", body, headers });

defects.title: Care instructions from the service are put into the page as HTML, so they can run a script
The service's guess is shown as fact, including whether the plant is safe for pets
"Watered today" uses the date in UTC, so it's wrong for part of every day outside UTC
Every render makes a new object URL for every photo and never releases them
Plants can be reordered only by dragging, with no way to do it by keyboard

locations.match: <li key={plant.id} draggable onDragStart={() => setDragging(plant.id ?? null)} onDrop={() => void moveTo(plant.position)}>

defects.title: Moving a plant gives it the same position as another, so the order becomes unpredictable
Photos are stored at full camera size, which fills the device's storage quota fast

locations.match: await db.plants.add({ name, room, position, ...(file === null ? {} : { photo: file }) });

defects.title: Muted text is too pale to read, and its colour isn't from the design tokens
